title: Amazon Conveyor EDA
description: Exploratory data analysis and root cause investigation of 9,686 SCADA alarm logs from Amazon's Pick to Rebin (P2R) conveyor system, identifying primary downtime drivers, bottleneck locations, and flow-balancing solutions.
businessProblem: Identify the primary causes of conveyor alarms and downtime within Amazon's Pick to Rebin (P2R) system across warehouse floors P2, P3, and P4 to reduce jams and protect shipping SLAs.
workflow: SCADA telemetry ingestion and schema validation across floors P2, P3, and P4
Timestamp parsing and alarm duration standardization (minutes and hours)
Alarm categorization into Congestion Indicators, Critical Faults, and Operational Events
Univariate and Pareto frequency distribution modeling
Spatial mapping to conveyor lines (2400, 2600, 2800) and photo-eye sensors
Floor-wise comparative analysis of alarm volume versus cumulative downtime
Root cause evaluation using Ishikawa (Fishbone) diagram and 5 Whys drill-down
Actionable engineering recommendations for dynamic routing and preventive maintenance
results: Congestion indicators account for 95.0% of all alarms, while Jam PEC 71 represents 88.05% of critical faults. P3 generates the most alarms (3,710), but P2 experiences the highest downtime (57.66 hours), dominated by a 66-hour cracked belt failure.
lessonsLearned: Alarm frequency does not equal operational severity; a single catastrophic belt crack caused 45% of total downtime. Integrating SCADA logs with spatial conveyor mapping pinpointed localized bottlenecks at PEC 71 on the 2600 line.
